limits: Identity cannot be determined from this spectrum. Only two non-substrate peaks (206.5 and 471.5 cm-1) are resolved, which is too few to match a layered compound. No reference library or literature access was available to compare against, so I did not claim a match.
Literature values in this report (Si 520.7 cm-1, SnS2 modes) are quoted from memory and were not verified here.
The 471.5 cm-1 peak sits on a broad background hump. It may be partly SiO2 (Si-O-Si bands near 440-490 cm-1 on SiO2/Si) or fluorescence; this cannot be separated with one spectrum.
Measured range is 60.3-1099.9 cm-1. Modes below 60 cm-1 and above 1100 cm-1 are not covered, so high-frequency and interlayer modes cannot be checked.
Noise is about 585 counts per point against a baseline of about 3400 counts. The 206.5 and 471.5 peaks are well above noise; the 323 cm-1 feature is marginal (about 3.5 sigma).
No cosmic-ray spikes were found (no point exceeds 5 sigma of local residual). Artifacts list is therefore empty.
Single unpolarized spectrum, so no polarization classification is possible.
Layer number, phase, defect level and strain cannot be inferred from this data.
